added_models.model: Genentech translational PK/PD-efficacy model of apitolisib (xenograft pAkt-to-tumour-growth link with allometric human PK)

engagement.model: Genentech translational PK/PD-efficacy model of apitolisib (xenograft pAkt-to-tumour-growth link with allometric human PK)
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading (Drug Metab Dispos, not in PMC). 2012 is a publication proxy: the prediction was made before first-in-human dosing (NCT00854152 started 2009-03). Apitolisib never reached an NDA, so model_filed is unknown.
engagement.quote: Parameters estimated from the pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic modeling of the MCF7-neo/HER2 xenograft data indicated that the GDC-0980 plasma concentration required for tumor stasis was approximately 0.5 μM.
engagement.note: Mouse PK/PD model tied tumour pAkt suppression to MCF7-neo/HER2 stasis at about 0.5 µM; no human PD comparison yet.
engagement.short: Xenograft pAkt-to-stasis model, untested in humans
engagement.judgement: Opens the in-silico track. The PK/PD model is a different system from the Wallin 2011 efficacy panel: it predicts a quantitative human exposure, clearance and dose, which the xenograft panel does not.

engagement.model: Genentech translational PK/PD-efficacy model of apitolisib (xenograft pAkt-to-tumour-growth link with allometric human PK)
engagement.magnitude_basis: constant pAkt inhibition needed for tumour stasis: 61% in 786-O xenografts vs 65% in phase 1 patients (platelet-rich plasma); 35-45% threshold in both
engagement.population: Advanced solid tumour phase 1 patients (NCT00854152, NCT00854126), 2-200 mg; not breast-specific
engagement.confidence_note: Full text read (PMC11315854). Both integrated models were fit in 2024 to phase 1 data public since Dolly 2016, so this is a retrodiction. Patients were mixed solid tumours, admitted under engagement's any-dosed-human rule. The concentration-to-pAkt IC50 differed 43-fold between tumour tissue (403 µg/L) and plasma (9.32 µg/L), which the authors attribute to matrix. Neither phase 1 posted registry results.
engagement.quote: Based on this relationship between targeted pAkt modulation and tumor shrinkage rate, it appeared that a constant pAkt inhibition of 61% and 65%, respectively, would be necessary to achieve tumor stasis in xenografts and patients.
engagement.note: Retrospective integrated PK-PD-efficacy models fit to xenograft and phase 1 data gave the same steep pAkt-to-tumour-shrinkage curve and stasis threshold.
engagement.short: Xenograft pAkt-efficacy curve reproduced in patients
engagement.judgement: Retro, not same: the clinical model was built after the phase 1 answer was known (decision 10). Direction and the stasis threshold agree within 2x; the 43-fold IC50 gap sits in the concentration-to-pAkt link, so the source's own framing is partial.

dose.model: Genentech translational PK/PD-efficacy model of apitolisib (xenograft pAkt-to-tumour-growth link with allometric human PK)
dose.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading (Drug Metab Dispos, not in PMC). 2012 is a publication proxy: the prediction was made before first-in-human dosing (NCT00854152 started 2009-03). Apitolisib never reached an NDA, so model_filed is unknown.
dose.quote: These parameters, combined with the predicted human pharmacokinetic profile, suggested that 55 mg once daily may be a clinically efficacious dose.
dose.note: Allometry predicted human CL 5.1 mL/min/kg and 55 mg once daily as the efficacious dose; no tolerability margin stated.
dose.reason: 55 mg never tolerated; no stated margin
dose.judgement: Later knowledge recorded without changing status: Dolly 2016 (doi 10.1158/1078-0432.CCR-15-2225) found MTD 50 mg and RP2D 40 mg once daily with fasting hyperglycaemia dose-limiting at 40 and 70 mg, and Moein 2024 population CL/F of 0.304 L/h/kg (5.07 mL/min/kg) matched the 5.1 mL/min/kg prediction. The predicted regimen was never a tolerated dose and the model stated no margin, so decision 16's no-margin row keeps the cell untested rather than contra with blocked_by toxicity.

efficacy.model: Genentech translational PK/PD-efficacy model of apitolisib (xenograft pAkt-to-tumour-growth link with allometric human PK)
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading (Drug Metab Dispos, not in PMC). 2012 is a publication proxy: the prediction was made before first-in-human dosing (NCT00854152 started 2009-03). Apitolisib never reached an NDA, so model_filed is unknown.
efficacy.quote: Parameters estimated from the pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic modeling of the MCF7-neo/HER2 xenograft data indicated that the GDC-0980 plasma concentration required for tumor stasis was approximately 0.5 μM.
efficacy.note: Model predicted tumour stasis at 55 mg once daily; FERGI arm B and the paclitaxel combination never reported a breast endpoint.
efficacy.judgement: The stasis prediction came from an MCF7-neo/HER2 breast xenograft, so it bears on this tile, but the only breast trials (NCT01437566 arm B, NCT01254526) completed without results and the 55 mg regimen was never given, so nothing can be scored.

considered_not_added: Gedatolisib (PF-05212384/PKI-587) Mallon 2011 xenografts paired with VIKTORIA-1 and its 2026 approval: gedatolisib is not among the tile's five members; the member list was not widened (checker lead 1).

Gedatolisib CDK4/6i- and ET-resistant ER+ PDX/PDO panel (Sci Transl Med 2025) and gedatolisib cell-line/xenograft panel (NPJ Breast Cancer 2024) paired with the phase 1b readouts: not a member drug (checker leads 2-3).

PF-04691502 PTEN-deficient PDX (Oncotarget 2017, PMID 29156674, doi 10.18632/oncotarget.19109): TNBC, ovarian and lung PDX dosed with PF-04691502 or gedatolisib plus chemotherapy or dacomitinib; the paper ends by deferring to the clinic, and no breast patient result for PF-04691502 exists (NCT01430585 Ki-67 arms never enrolled), so no patient comparison.

Luminal androgen receptor TNBC PDX (Theranostics 2020, PMID 32042320, doi 10.7150/thno.36182): the dual PI3K/mTOR inhibitor dosed was PF-04691502 (full text names PF-04691502, buparlisib, AZD8055, AZD2014); the 329-patient TNBC cohort was genotyped only, never dosed, so no patient comparison.

Eichhorn 2008 NKI BT474 shRNA/PIK3CA-mutant lapatinib-resistance model (draft efficacy entry 1): a re-keying of an existing entry from bez235-novartis-xenografts to its own model_id, and no new patient comparison was found (no breast dactolisib efficacy endpoint ever read), so it stays an edit to the draft outside this file.

Dactolisib versus everolimus randomized phase II in pancreatic NET (Oncologist 2018, doi 10.1634/theoncologist.2017-0144): patient-side safety data importable to the existing bez235-novartis-xenografts track, not a new model system.
Taselisib phase 1 (Cancer Discov 2017, PMID 28331003) states PIK3CA-mutant xenograft to patient concordance: PI3K-alpha-selective, not a member of this class.

sfRon-expressing breast cancer PDX with PI3K inhibitors (Clin Cancer Res 2015, PMID 26289070) surfaced in the BEZ235 PDX search: combination PDX work with no patient comparison; whether a member drug was dosed was not verified.

No patient-derived organoid, ex-vivo explant, human genetic, or co-clinical PDX comparison surfaced for dactolisib, voxtalisib, bimiralisib or apitolisib in breast cancer (searches 3, 9, 11); voxtalisib and bimiralisib hits were lymphoma, glioma and phase 1 papers only.

No in-silico or PK/PD human-dose prediction surfaced for PF-04691502, voxtalisib, bimiralisib or dactolisib (searches 4, 8, 10); the only published translational PK/PD prediction in the class is the apitolisib one added here.

Moein 2024 could alternatively be read as a new entry on the existing gdc0980-genentech-xenografts track; it is kept separate because the Salphati 2012 PK/PD model is an in-silico system making a quantitative exposure, clearance and dose prediction the efficacy panel never made (track identity rule for this run).
